clues: Because as few as 10 to 50 bacteria can cause severe illness via inhalation, nations studied this as a biological weapon. Japan tested it involuntarily on civilian and military prisoners in occupied Manchuria during WWII

In 1978 and again in 2000, local landscapers and residents in Martha's Vineyard came down with severe, airborne forms of this disease. Investigators discovered that landscapers were accidentally running over infected rabbit carcasses or nests, aerosolizing the bacteria into the air

In 1911, Dr. McCoy was investigating what he thought was an outbreak of bubonic plague among local ground squirrels in Tulare County, California. He was able to identify that it was a new causal organism and Dr. Edward Francis proved that this bacterium was the source of several regional human illnesses.

Also known as Devil's Breath, this potent plant alkaloid is derived from nightshade family plants and has been used since antiquity. In medieval European folklore, this was one of the primary ingredients in 'flying ointments' used by witches and folk healers where extracts were mixed with animal fats and applied topically to mucous membranes. This would cause severe delirium and vivid realistic hallucinations of flying.

Because high doses cause confusion and hinder memory formation while sometimes making people talkative, researchers hoped it would compel honesty. Extensive testing proved that it does not compel truthfulness but instead induces severe delirium, hallucinations, urinary retention, mydriasis, and hyperthermia
This is a muscarinic antagonist used to treat motion sickness and post operative nausea and vomiting. It is commonly prescribed as a transdermal patch.

This is actually derived from a group of flowering plants in the legume family. It has been used medically at least since the 700s AD and is originally native to North Africa, the Middle East, and India
One of the few herbal remedies approved by the FDA for over-the-counter use, it can harmlessly turn your urine a reddish-brown or pinkish color.

Because it is a stimulant laxative, it forcibly irritates and contracts the colonic muscles. Over time, chronic daily use causes the colon to rely on this trigger where the body forgets how to move waste naturally

A manifestation of underlying illness, ancient therapies for this physical examination finding included placing live pigeons on a patient's abdomen or even swallowing lice harvested from one's own head to restore humor balances.

The medical term for this comes from a Greek word for the Eurasian golden oriole. Ancient practitioners believed that if an affected person gazed at this yellow bird, the bird would die taking the illness with it
This affects roughly 60% of full-term and 80% of premature newborns. Most cases resolve on their own although more severe cases are treated with blue phototherapy.

Humans are not the only victims of this disease. Marine mammals, particularly dolphins and whales, are highly susceptible with a near-zero survival rate. It typically presents as an occult infection, spreading through the respiratory tracts until it becomes fatal
The first human case described was in 1876. An autopsy of a cancer patient revealed a hemorrhagic infarct in the right lung containing hyphae and sporangia
Typically obtained from environmental exposure such as inhalation or ingestion, this angioinvasive fungus primarily targets immunocompromised individuals or those with poorly controlled diabetes.
